summary: Kalmegh dry extract is prepared from Andrographis paniculata, the bitter Ayurvedic herb known as the 'King of Bitters'. Its principal active constituent is the diterpene lactone andrographolide, which has anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties. It is used traditionally and in some clinical studies for symptomatic relief of the common cold and uncomplicated upper respiratory tract infections. It is a herbal supplement, not an approved pharmaceutical drug; doses are standardised to andrographolide content.

Reduction of cold symptoms (sore throat, cough, rhinorrhoea, malaise) - traditional/herbal use

moa: The active diterpenoid lactone andrographolide exerts anti-inflammatory effects (modulation of NF-kB signalling and pro-inflammatory cytokines) and immunomodulatory/immunostimulant activity, with some antipyretic and antioxidant actions reported. These effects are proposed to reduce the severity and duration of upper respiratory symptoms rather than to act as a direct antimicrobial cure.

preg: Avoid in pregnancy. Andrographis is traditionally contraindicated and animal data and traditional use raise concern for abortifacient/anti-fertility effects; safety in human pregnancy is not established.
lact: Avoid during breastfeeding owing to insufficient safety data.
renal: No established dose adjustment; human data in renal impairment are limited, so use cautiously.
hepatic: No established dose adjustment; use cautiously given limited safety data and potential for hypersensitivity-type reactions.

pearls: Herbal/Ayurvedic supplement, NOT an FDA-approved drug - information drawn from herbal monographs, supplement references and clinical study data; product quality and standardisation vary between brands
Andrographolide is the marker/active constituent; dose by standardised andrographolide content rather than crude extract weight
Has immunostimulant activity - caution in autoimmune disease and with immunosuppressants
Avoid in pregnancy and breastfeeding; possible reversible effects on male fertility with prolonged/high use
Should not replace evaluation or treatment of significant or bacterial infection
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it. Because it is used for short-term symptom relief, simply resume the usual schedule rather than doubling up.
overdose: Excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal upset (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea), loss of appetite and fatigue. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive. Discontinue the product and seek medical advice for marked or persistent symptoms or any allergic reaction.
